question: to the Commission Ştefan Muşoiu (S&D) Subject:

Current geopolitical and geostrategic developments make it increasingly likely that the European Union will face renewed migratory pressure in the form of migrants from Muslim states affected by the war in the Middle East. The International Organization for Migration has drawn attention to the risk of a long-term migratory crisis and to the fact that in Lebanon over one million people have been displaced and shelter facilities are close to full capacity. Given these circumstances, the European Union should be incorporating the lessons learned from the previous migration crisis in 2015 into its current policies, and hence furnish concrete support measures for third countries and the most appropriate responses for Member States, through preventive measures and rapid response mechanisms for managing a significant influx of refugees. In this regard, can the Commission clarify what prevention plan it has decided upon for managing a foreseeable new and larger wave of refugees heading for the European Union, what updated EU-level decisions have been taken as regards a long-term migratory crisis and in what ways it intends to support frontline states and avoid a repetition of the situations that arose during the 2015 migrant crisis?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.5.2026) The Commission is closely monitoring developments in the Middle East and is supporting partner countries, including through cooperation with international organisations. There are currently no indications of increased cross-border movements towards the EU. Preparedness is ensured through the implementation of a comprehensive migration crisis response framework. Member States are responsible for contingency planning concerning border and migration management, which is complemented at EU level by coordination and support measures, including the EU Migration Preparedness and Crisis Blueprint Network1, the EU Civil Protection Mechanism, the operational and technical support of EU agencies, and flexible EU funding. The Commission recognises that Member States at EU external borders may be particularly exposed. The Commission is therefore providing targeted support, including reinforced operational deployments of EU agencies, to help ensure an effective migration management system and it is ready to step up assistance if needed. The Pact on Migration and Asylum2 offers a comprehensive approach and firm but fair rules to manage migration in a spirit of responsibility and solidarity. This includes strengthening preparedness, ensuring a coordinated crisis response and embedding migration in international partnerships, including the possibility to adapt to exceptional migration-related circumstances, as set out in the Crisis and Force Majeure Regulation3.
1 Commission Recommendation (EU) 2020/1366 of 23 September 2020 on an EU mechanism for preparedness

and management of crises related to migration, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reco/2020/1366/oj/eng. 2 https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/pact-migration-and-asylum_en. 3 Regulation (EU) 2024/1359 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 addressing situations of crisis and force majeure in the field of migration and asylum and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1147, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1359/oj/eng.
